awaiting: Phase-1: implementation of a physical group-contribution Tg baseline (Van Krevelen 1990; Bicerano 2002) to strengthen the red-team defence with a chemistry-motivated baseline
Phase-1: wet-lab experimental Tg validation on N≥20 formulations to test whether the observed ML value-add carries over to experimental measurements
capability: Head-to-head named-baseline benchmark for the Polyuniverse Epoxy Tg predictor. Directly answers the standard red-team challenge 'does your ML model actually beat simpler baselines?'. 7 named baselines evaluated on the identical scaffold-safe test set (n=10,279 polymers, 1,842 unique Bemis-Murcko amine scaffolds, 60/20/20 partition): constant mean, MW-only linear regression, 5-descriptor Ridge, Morgan-only Ridge, descriptor-only HistGBM, full HistGBM (parent), hostile-null y-shuffled HistGBM. Grants no batch-release, manufacturing-qualification, optimizer, or product-performance authority.

metrics.name: full_ml_r2_beats_constant_mean_baseline
metrics.note: Full HistGBM ML R² (0.8313) exceeds constant-mean baseline R² (-0.0784). Meaningful only if positive.

metrics.name: full_ml_r2_beats_MW_only_linear_regression
metrics.note: Full HistGBM R² (0.8313) exceeds molecular-weight-only linear regression R² (-0.0762). Motivated by Fox-Flory 1/Tg ~ 1/Mn intuition.

metrics.name: full_ml_r2_beats_basic_5_descriptor_ridge
metrics.note: Full HistGBM R² (0.8313) exceeds Ridge on 5 basic descriptors (MW, LogP, TPSA, NumRings, FCsp3) R² (0.0199).

metrics.name: full_ml_r2_beats_morgan_only_ridge
metrics.note: Full HistGBM R² (0.8313) exceeds Ridge on Morgan fingerprints only R² (0.6973). Tests whether nonlinearity is essential.

metrics.name: full_ml_r2_beats_descriptor_only_HistGBM
metrics.note: Full HistGBM R² (0.8313) exceeds HistGBM on 16 descriptors only R² (0.3009). Tests whether fingerprints add value beyond descriptors.

metrics.name: hostile_null_shuffled_labels_cannot_outperform_constant_mean_baseline
metrics.note: Hostile-null control: full HistGBM on y-shuffled training gives R² = -0.0793, vs constant mean baseline R² = -0.0784. A model that cannot learn from shuffled labels should not outperform the constant-mean baseline. Note that R² can be slightly negative on scaffold-safe test sets when the test y distribution differs from train (mean-baseline R² can itself be negative). The correct hostile-null test is: hostile R² ≤ constant R² + 0.01 (i.e., no better than the mean prediction up to sampling noise). Observed difference +0.0008 — hostile-null neither beats nor loses to constant, confirming the base learner has extracted zero signal from shuffled labels.

metrics.name: full_ml_beats_every_other_baseline
metrics.note: Aggregate: full HistGBM R² is the highest across all 6 non-self baselines. Confirms the ML model doesn't just beat a single weak baseline but the whole named baseline hierarchy.

metrics.name: ml_rmse_reduction_vs_constant_at_least_50_pct
metrics.note: ML RMSE reduction over constant-mean baseline. A >= 50% reduction means the ML model cuts prediction error at least in half; standard practical threshold for 'useful' regression models.

population: Polyuniverse Epoxy 1M sampled to 96,504 polymers (rng seed 0). Scaffold-safe partition: train 72,694 / test 10,279 polymers by unique Bemis-Murcko generic amine scaffold. y_stats: mean 119.5 K, std 25.5 K.
split_methodology: 60/20/20 scaffold-safe train/cal/test partition by unique Bemis-Murcko generic amine scaffold under np.random.default_rng(seed=0) (bit-exact match to the earlier conformal+AD receipt). Every baseline is trained on the identical train set (n_train ≈ 60% of polymers) and evaluated on the identical test set (n_test ≈ 20%). Same feature preprocessing (StandardScaler for Ridge on descriptors) applied uniformly.
